title: UFO material seemed to communicate telepathically with Malmgren
summary: Jesse Michels tells of UFO material seemed to communicate telepathically with Malmgren, about 1962 at Mexico (no place named), and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: when Harold was holding the UFO pieces Lawrence G had given him, they seemed to [music] telepathically communicate with him. He heard words in his head when he felt the pieces.
And then he goes, they show him the UFO pieces. He feels the the debris. He feels this anomalous debris. It speaks to him telepathically
tellings.difference: Places the handling at Sandia/Kirtland rather than Los Alamos.
tellings.link_reason: Same 1962 account of UFO pieces from Gise seeming to speak telepathically to Malmgren when he handled them.

as_told.title: Malmgren shown UFO debris at Sandia that spoke to him telepathically
as_told.place_text: Sandia, Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico

tellings.quote: know, I interviewed a guy, Harold Malmgren, who basically on his deathbed said that he held in his hands UFO material from that came out of the plume of a blast from Operation Bluegill Triple Prime, and it was given to him by Jeff Bezos's maternal grandfather, Lawrence Preston Geise, at Sandia National Labs and Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico.
tellings.difference: Says the material came from the Bluegill Triple Prime blast plume and puts the handover at Sandia/Kirtland rather than Los Alamos; it does not mention telepathy and frames it as a deathbed claim.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Harold Malmgren handling UFO pieces that Lawrence Gise gave him in New Mexico in 1962.

as_told.title: Malmgren held UFO material from the Bluegill Triple Prime blast plume
as_told.place_text: Sandia National Labs / Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico; Pacific test site

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on a story from Harald Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, and his daughter Pippa. According to Michels, in 1962 a man named Lawrence Gise handed Malmgren pieces said to come from a UFO, and as Malmgren held them he heard words in his head, as if the material were speaking to him by telepathy, meaning mind to mind. Michels places this at Los Alamos, the US weapons laboratory in New Mexico, in one telling and at the Sandia and Kirtland military sites in New Mexico in another; if true, it would mean the debris was not just strange metal but something able to communicate.
